description: Negative fixture that tests the JUDGEMENT rather than the filter (#282). 20 kernels of 200ms separated by 19 gaps of 2ms: 38.00ms idle across a 4038.00ms span, 0.9411% (measured, not derived — an earlier version of this label stated the intended 40ms/4040ms/0.99% and was wrong). The gaps exceed the 1ms min_gap_ns floor, so unlike healthy_1pct.sqlite the pipeline actually sees and weighs them. The correct answer is still that ~1% is not recoverable.
source: Generated so the gap size clears the reporting floor while the idle share stays near one percent. The sibling healthy_1pct.sqlite measures 0.9876%; this one 0.9411%. They are close but NOT identical — 19 gaps between 20 kernels rather than a round 20 — so the pair isolates gap size, not a fixed share.
why_this_matters: healthy_1pct.sqlite passes partly because its 10us gaps are below min_gap_ns and never reach a threshold at all. That guards against the floor drifting down, but it does not prove the tool declines to call a small-but-visible idle share a bottleneck. This fixture does.

expect.note: Compute-bound, as with its sibling. Not gated.

must_not.note: No NCCL activity exists here; any communication finding is a false positive.
0.99% idle must not reach warning severity. The gaps remain visible as informational observations, but must not compete with material bottlenecks.
